title: Earl Bostic runs Kermit Scott off the stand
summary: At a Harlem club Bostic sat in and called Eliza in E flat, rising a half step each chorus, which drove Kermit Scott off his own job.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Look, Earl Bostick run Kermit Scott off his job. You know how New York musicians are. Earl was at Menton's at 118th and 7th Avenue, and he was standing around the post listening to him play and asked him, say, could I sit in one? Kermit said yeah. Big guy -- and Earl was very timid in (inaudible).
So he told the piano player, said play Eliza in E flat, and each chorus go up half a step round the cycle. He's changing keys on him. Kermit, as bad as he was, he
walked off his own job. You didn't see him no more that night. Kermit Scott (inaudible).
He was a good (inaudible) too, wasn't he?
Sure, he was. Out of Beaumont, Texas.
He's out of Texas too? Oh, I didn't know that.

I knew Kermit very well. But just to show you, though, you don't disrespect and you can't judge a book by its cover. Just respect people. You get along better. Nobody get that big, but he got big with (inaudible) run him off his own job. He didn't want to come back on the stand anymore, Liza -- and the tempo was (clapping).
Who moved up a step, the piano player or -- or Earl?
Who moved up a step with each chorus?
Well, he'd be telling the piano player. In other words, after each chorus --
-- you change. You go up a half a step, and that go around a circle of -- cycle of 13 keys.
And it was Earl who called it that way.

Earl called it that way, and he makes the modulation, and he go a half a step up until he can revert right back to E flat and take it out. He was a master. He knew his instrument. He could play. But he couldn't understand it. But that's what he was doing, and the general public don't know it. He was a musician's musician. Musician can love it, but the paying customer, say, now what is he doing?
